anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Mis-tuned engine parameters (memory, parallelism, checkpoints, etc.) that distort resource usage patterns and introduce artificial bottlenecks independent of true hardware limits.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Host CPU cores are genuinely saturated or oversubscribed by database processes, causing elevated run-queue delays and system-wide latency.

When both root causes coexist the system presents a confusing mixture of symptoms: CPU utilisation hovers at or near 100 %, yet individual sessions may simultaneously report waits that suggest they are "spinning" or throttled by configuration limits (e.g., small work-memory forcing excessive batch-loop processing, aggressive parallel-worker allocation leading to context-switch storms, or checkpoint storms producing bursts of log-flush CPU). Wait-event histograms show an interleaving of CPU-bound activity (CPU time, scheduler waits) and configuration-induced waits (buffer-pin, log-write, flush-queue), and performance counters may oscillate as background processes kick in late due to CPU starvation. Response-time spikes appear across both read and write paths; even after workload subsides, recovery and autovacuum/cleanup tasks lag because mis-sized maintenance workers cannot acquire CPU.

Causally, sub-optimal configuration settings inflate the amount of CPU work per transaction (e.g., too-small caches trigger extra page decompression and checksum verification, over-parallel plans multiply worker threads, tight checkpoint intervals force frequent flush bookkeeping). This artificial demand pushes the host CPU past sustainable limits, producing a true CPU Resource Anomaly. In turn, sustained CPU saturation amplifies the negative impact of the bad settings: background writers miss their cadence, causing larger and more expensive checkpoints, while worker shortages lead the optimizer to fall back to inefficient serial plans that again raise per-query CPU cost. The feedback loop between poor configuration and CPU exhaustion deepens latency, obscures which layer is primary, and can ultimately stall throughput or trigger failover mechanisms.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the timeout in seconds for attempts to acquire metadata locks.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_wait_timeout while attempting to acquire a metadata lock.
entry.workload_impact: The metadata lock acquisition fails and the statement does not proceed.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
